newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall in volatile reaction to Fed decision.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall in volatile reaction to Fed decision.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks ended lower Tuesday as the Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady drew a classic buy-on-the-rumour and sell-on-the-news market response.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 20.71 points to 5,874.03 just one day after closing at a record of 5.894.74.
The blue-chip index also was weighed down by a sell-off in the stock of AT&T, which tumbled 5-3/4 to 51-1/2 on an earnings warning.
"We had a negative surprise from one of the bellwether stocks of all time," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,206 to 1,074 on heavy volume of 457 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The Fed's announcement in mid-afternoon initially triggered a rally, sending the Dow up more than 30 points. A wave of selling soon followed, sending the Dow sliding more than 40 points before it reversed course yet again just moments before the close.

The Fed's decision, which had been anxiously awaited amid concern that inflation was building up, left the key federal funds rate that banks charge each other for overnight loans unchanged at 5-1/4 percent. The central bank also held the discount rate, which the Fed charges banks, at 5 percent.
Some analysts had expected the central bank to lift rates by a token one quarter percentage point, which would have been the first hike in 1-1/2 years.
Analysts said the market interpreted the Fed's inaction as a delay of an inevitable increase after the November elections.
"Economists and traders are trying to distill all the news and ramifications of the Fed's inaction," said Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst at Janney, Montgomery Scott.
"We had a knee-jerk rally and are consolidating to inflationary implications. It's a positive. The volatility is helping to keep excesses minimised," he said.
Analysts cited a number of reasons for the choppy finish.
"The rally in stocks and bonds pulled back partly due to the dollar," said David Shulman, chief equity strategist at Salomon Brothers, noting that the dollar fell sharply on the Fed's decision.

In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond rose 14/32 and its yield fell to 6.99 percent from 7.02 percent at Monday's close. The dollar was at 1.5020 German marks in late trading, down from 1.5127 marks on Monday. The currency fell to 109.05 Japanese yen vs. 109.92 yen.
Much of the afternoon seesaw activity in the Dow index was driven by a series of massive programme trades.

According to Birinyi Associates Inc., a buy programme initiated just after news of the Fed's vote added about 30 points to the Dow. That programme was followed almost immediately by a sell programme that wiped out those gains.

Early in the session, the market was hit by a stunning profit warning from AT&T Corp. whose stock fell 5-5/8 to 51-1/2 after saying that competition in its key long-distance telephone market would likely result in profit shortfalls for the second half of the year.

Among individual stocks, leading semiconductor maker Texas Instruments surged 5-5/8 to 57-3/8 after Montgomery Securities upgraded the stock to buy from hold. Also helping Texas Instruments was news that spot prices for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips have risen. Fellow DRAM maker Micron Technologies Inc. gained 3-1/2 to 31-1/2.

Several initial public offerings drew strong buying. Cross-Continent Auto, which operates six franchised automobile dealerships, climbed 6 to 20 in its debut. Hot Topic Inc., an apparel maker, rose 8-1/8 to 26-1/8 on its first day.
Apparel designer Mossimo extended its losses, falling 3-1/2 to 30-1/2 after sinking 6-7/8 Monday on its warning that its earnings would fall far short of analysts' expectations.
GMIS Inc. soared 6-3/16 to 23-5/16 after agreeing to be acquired by HBO & Co. HBO & Co. fell 1-1/4 to 62-1/2.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 3.80 points to 1,215.27.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 0.87 to 685.61. The American Stock Exchange index dipped 0.22 to 563.40
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.28 to 365.23. The average share was down 3 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,723.487 down 0.377 or 0.01 percent.
